thread.title: Markets Now: Dow Finds Its Mojo, Gains 298 Points - Barron's

author: barrons.com
title: Markets Now: Dow Finds Its Mojo, Gains 298 Points - Barron's
text:
Updated May 4, 2018 1:21 p.m. ET Want to know why the Dow Jones Industrial Average is doing what it's doing? Check back here for a semi-live look at the volatile markets from Barron's reporters.
2:54 p.m. The Dow is now up 386.24, or 1.61%, to 24,316.39, as the market extends its gains. Apple (AAPL) is the big winning component so far; with an hour left in the trading day, shares are up nearly 4%. We've noted that despite the iPhone X being the most expensive smartphone on the market, it still sold more units than any other model in the latest quarter.
Interestingly, the next biggest mover in the Dow is McDonald's (MCD), which is up 3.14%. Hmm, maybe that's a reference to apple pi? — Ed Lin
1:10 p.m. Break out the champagne! Break out the Dow! The index is up 298.23, or 1.25%, at 24,228.38. The market isn't necessarily celebrating the OK-ness of the latest jobs report, but what the data set up for later in 2018. "April job gains were moderate, with signs that unfavorable weather weighed on the labor market," Morgan Stanley economist Ellen Zentner wrote in a research report. "Wage growth slowed, driven by diminishing contributions from high- and middle-wage industries. With the unemployment rate at 3.9%, we except wages will gradually reaccelerate over the course of the year." — Ed Lin
10:15 a.m. The Dow has wrung out the red and is now up 48.74, or 0.20%, at 23,978.89. It's hard to be negative amid strong earnings reports, low unemployment and unseasonably warm weather. — Ed Lin
Illustration: Bloomberg News 8:32 a.m. Good call from High Frequency Economics' Jim O'Sullivan . U.S. payrolls grew by 164,000 jobs in April, below economist predictions for 188,000. The good news: The unemployment rate fell to 3.9%, the first time it's been below 4% since 2000 . Wages rose 2.6% from a year ago but just 0.1% from the previous month. Here's how Thomas Simons , senior money market economist at Jefferies , summed up the report:
Payrolls came in weaker than expected, though there were 30+K upward revisions to the March data. Taken together, the employment data with the revisions is close to expectations. More disappointing is the 0.1% increase in AHE, which was likely weighed down to some extent by weather and also by the fact that the 15th of the month, when many workers are paid, was NOT included in the survey week. This calendar phenomenon has had an inconsistent negative impact on the AHE data when it has popped up.
S&P 500 futures have fallen 0.2%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have declined 43 points, or 0.2%. Nasdaq Composite futures have dropped 0.3%. Dow Drops 40 Points as Payrolls Loom 6:38 a.m. No deal between the U.S. and China means no gain for the major market indexes this morning. S&P 500 futures have fallen 0.2%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have declined 40 points, or 0.2%. Nasdaq Composite futures have dropped 0.2%. China and the U.S. finished their trade discussions but didn't reach any conclusions , which means tariffs might still be happening. "Futures are slightly lower thanks to a lack of a clear, positive headline from the U.S./China summit," writes Sevens Report's Tom Essaye . But with April payrolls data being released at 8:30 a.m. this morning , that loss could easily be erased if the numbers show are not too hot and not too cold, or could cause it to get worse if they suggest a pickup in inflation.
Economists expect the U.S. economy to have added 188,000 jobs in April, but some aren't so sure that's reachable. "We see downside risk for this week's payrolls data..." writes High Frequency Economics' Jim O'Sullivan . "In particular, we expect seasonal hiring to be held back by winter-like weather continuing into early April in many parts of the country." We'll find out at 8:30 if he's right. — Ben Levisohn
